listing.name: Master of Orion (1oom (vanilla branch))
listing.summary: Research listing. Upstream route: Native recreation with original v1.3 LBX input and Windows RC package. Limits: Default branch warns no longer developed; select vanilla branch/current lineage and heed save compatibility. Upstream platforms: Windows release-candidate package on vanilla lineage; desktop source builds documented. Selected Windows CPU architecture unknown in frozen evidence; discontinued default branch differs. Original data: Legally own Master of Orion version 1.3 and supply its original LBX files. This 1oom target does not establish compatibility with a different original-game version; separately preserve its documented save-compatibility limitations. Portcove setup/gameplay not verified.

steps.title: Choose the actual vanilla RC5 lineage
steps.instruction: Use a permitted completed Windows copy of the reviewed 1oom vanilla-RC5 beta/testing package and your own Master of Orion version 1.3 LBX data. The exact tag and current master-vanilla-beta-RC5 branch resolve to a956a6f73f75e6cd26b701afcd04bd4973650520. The discontinued default branch/latest v1.11.9 and the separately referenced newer SourceCraft project do not inherit this guide. A provider prerelease flag of false does not remove the beta/RC/testing scope. No version pin or automatic managed replacement of this lineage is offered.

steps.title: Select the native graphical player
steps.instruction: Select the prepared graphical 1oom_classic_sdl2.exe (or the actual prepared SDL1 graphical variant), keeping the complete companion DLLs and chosen MOO data directory. Do not select lbxview, saveconv, the command-line demonstration, a DOS executable or emulator. Retain established -data ABS and -user ABS as separate literal arguments when configured; they select distinct data and user roots.

steps.title: Preserve original-format slots and configuration
steps.instruction: Preserve the whole creating runtime, all LBX originals, CONFIG.MOO and every SAVE*.GAM or 1oom_save*.bin slot in the actual user root. Selected Windows source defaults that root to the working directory, not an invented literal User subfolder; -user can redirect it. Original-format saves are enabled by default and use the original MOO slot names, so running inside the original installation can overwrite those existing slots. Keep an independent recoverable copy before running/changing engines. Source support for a format is not observed backward compatibility or permission to migrate saves.

steps.title: Review the prepared player and launch details
steps.instruction: Finish setup with the project’s tools, then start and quit the permitted copy you intend to add. Keep its game executable, working folder and supported launch arguments. Review those details in Portcove and agree to launch them, then choose Play separately. Adding a copy does not confirm its original game files, gameplay or save compatibility.

steps.title: Retain upstream replacement and external ownership
steps.instruction: Close every running copy of the game before changing files. Keep the working game version and every original-file, profile and data location it uses. Update it with the project’s tools, then review and select the changed executable in Portcove. You manage setup, replacement, file changes, data migration and recovery. Portcove monitors the process you selected; it does not restrict file access or prevent other copies from running. Removing the registration leaves external files in place. This route does not offer Portcove downloads, setup, updates, backups, rollback, data migration or external-file deletion.

warnings: Use only a copy and components you are already permitted to use. Engine licensing does not grant original-game, music, mod, middleware or redistribution rights.
Before changing versions, keep a copy of the working game and every data and profile folder it uses. Another executable may use those same folders.
